text: Codex runs under its own permission profile (#153's step 5, option 1 of four), chosen by @gitdek over a container, a separate macOS user and a sandbox of our own. Codex's commands can read only the workspace, the system's own files and the toolchains, write only in the workspace, and reach no network; Codex's sign-in lives in a home of its own outside everything they can read, so they can't read it either. Codex's own connection to its service isn't sandboxed, and neither is Invariant's MCP server, so the agent still thinks, and checks its work with the gate, check and test tools. Codex jobs run one at a time, since runs sharing one sign-in can break each other's token refresh. The profile is a Codex beta, so the watcher checks at start that it holds: a command under it can't read a file in Codex's home.
